title: Route Guards
summary: Protect routes with guards — like blocking pages behind a login.
heading: Route Guards

blocks.text: A guard is a small function the router runs before (or after) navigating. It decides whether the user is allowed to go there — for example, blocking a dashboard unless the user is logged in.

sections.title: Generating a guard with the CLI

blocks.text: Don't write the file by hand — let the CLI scaffold it. ng generate guard creates the guard file (and its test).

blocks.label: Terminal
blocks.code:
ng generate guard auth
# short version:
ng g guard auth

blocks.text: The CLI then asks which kind of guard you want — pick one (or more) with the spacebar:

blocks.label: prompt
blocks.code:
? Which type of guard would you like to create?
  ◯ CanActivate
  ◯ CanActivateChild
  ◯ CanDeactivate
  ◯ CanMatch

blocks.text: Choosing CanActivate generates a ready-to-fill functional guard:

blocks.label: auth.guard.ts (generated)

blocks.text: It also creates auth.guard.spec.ts. Now you just fill in the logic — that's the next step.
A modern guard is just a function of type CanActivateFn. Inside it you can inject services. Return true to allow, or a UrlTree (from router.parseUrl) to redirect.

blocks.label: auth.guard.ts

sections.title: Attaching the guard to a route

blocks.text: List the guard in the route's canActivate array. You can attach several guards.

blocks.label: routes

blocks.text: Now visiting /dashboard while logged out bounces the user to /login.

layers.title: canActivate
layers.detail: Can the user enter this route? (auth, roles)

layers.title: canActivateChild
layers.detail: Same check, applied to a route's children

layers.title: canDeactivate
layers.detail: Can the user leave? (warn about unsaved changes)

blocks.label: canDeactivate example

blocks.text: Guards show up all over real apps. A few you'll meet often:

layers.title: Authentication
layers.detail: Require a logged-in user before showing a page; otherwise redirect to /login.

layers.title: Roles & permissions
layers.detail: Let only admins reach /admin; send others to a 'not allowed' page.

layers.title: Unsaved changes
layers.detail: canDeactivate: warn before leaving a half-filled form.

layers.title: Onboarding / setup
layers.detail: Force new users through a setup step before the main app.

layers.title: Subscription / paywall
layers.detail: Block premium routes unless the plan is active.

layers.title: Feature flags
layers.detail: Hide a route that isn't enabled yet for this user.

blocks.label: role guard example

blocks.text: A guard can also return a Promise or Observable of boolean/UrlTree — handy when the check needs a server call (e.g. verifying a token).

items: A guard is a function the router runs to allow or block navigation.
